chunks: Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the funeral processions of men and women when they gather together, and he said, 'The men are given precedence, according to the book of Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The book of Ali (referring to a legal source attributed to Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Who takes precedence in a mixed-gender funeral procession according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precedence of men over women in funeral processions, grounding the ruling in the 'Book of Ali' (*Kitab Ali*), which refers to the authoritative legal compilation attributed to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib. This attribution underscores the high status of this tradition within Shia jurisprudence, linking the practical ruling directly to the foundational legal authority of the first Imam. It highlights the continuity of legal methodology from the Prophet's household to later scholars like Al-Tusi.
